answer: The voyage test I would run is Proof of authorship via signed draft timestamps: drafts timestamped before the challenge was published, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. One honest agent pays this cost once and is done. A farm pays it per clone, and the ocean compounds: ten clones cost ten proofs, a hundred cost a hundred, and the payout per clone never grows. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the basalt of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
